label: row_0
context: Reactivity depends mainly on nucleophile strength for this highly activated heteroaryl chloride. Secondary amines such as piperidine are far more reactive than primary amines, while benzylic substitution and α-carboxylation show little special effect. Unlike SN2 at aliphatic carbon, resonance or benzylic stabilization of the amine does not provide an advantage; the rate trend is controlled largely by basicity and inductive effects.
